label: copy-phase input u (fed-back u), strongest in short sequences / u-u repeats
explanation: Fires only on copy-phase steps whose input is the token u (the model's own fed-back u): every activation has in_tok == u and phase == copy (recall 1.0), never in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other input token. But only ~12% of copy-phase u inputs fire. Firing is more likely and stronger in short sequences (L = 3-5), early recall positions (recall_idx 2-3, i.e. u as the 2nd/3rd original token), and when the next token to output is also u (u u repeats); the top activations are all of the form X u u ... <DEL> X [u]. Weak or absent on u inputs late in long sequences (L >= 7, recall_idx >= 5). The predicate adding (L <= 5 or out_tok == u) gets dev F1 ~0.50 and mass recall ~0.85; the residual gating looks graded rather than a crisp rule.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: u, -, h, s, j, t; least: d, k, c, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: u, 2, 3, p, v, g; least: l, -, a, z); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, L=3 & t=4, recall_idx=2.
